p.src: Jia Lian went to Lady Wang and told her everything. The next day, he went to the ministry and completed all the necessary arrangements. On returning, he again called on Lady Wang and reported what he had arranged at the Ministry of Personnel. Lady Wang asked, “Have you made quite certain of it? If that is indeed how matters stand, your uncle will be pleased, and the whole family can set their minds at ease. How could he ever manage an appointment in the provinces! Had he not been impeached and recalled in this way, those scoundrels might even have cost him his life!” “How could you know about that, Aunt?” asked Jia Lian. Lady Wang replied, “Ever since your second uncle received his provincial appointment, he has not brought a single coin home; instead, a good deal has been taken from the family coffers. Just look at the men who accompanied your uncle. They had scarcely been away any time before their young wives at home began decking themselves out in gold and silver. Surely that means their husbands were lining their pockets behind your uncle’s back? Your uncle simply let them carry on as they pleased. If they had caused a scandal, not only would he have lost his own office, but even the hereditary honors of our ancestors might have been revoked.” “You are quite right, Aunt,” said Jia Lian. When I first heard that he had been impeached, I was terribly frightened, and only felt relieved after waiting until I had learned the truth. I too hope that Uncle will hold a post in the capital and spend a few peaceful, comfortable years there; only then can his good name remain secure for the rest of his life. Even Grandmother will be reassured when she hears, provided you break the news to her gently.” “I know,” said Lady Wang. But you must go and inquire further.”

p.src: Jia Lian assented and was just about to leave when an old servant woman from Aunt Xue’s household hurried in. She entered Lady Wang’s inner room without even stopping to pay her respects and blurted out, “Our mistress sent me to tell her ladyship here that something terrible has happened in our house—there has been another dreadful disturbance.” On hearing this, Lady Wang asked, “What has happened?” “It is terrible, simply terrible!” the old woman repeated. Lady Wang gave an exasperated snort. “You muddleheaded creature! If it is urgent, then tell us plainly what it is!” The old woman said, “Our Second Master is away, and there is not a single man in the house. What are we to do now that this has happened? We beg you, madam, to send a few of the gentlemen over to take matters in hand.” Lady Wang could make no sense of this and demanded impatiently, “What exactly do you need the gentlemen to go there for?” “Our eldest young mistress is dead,” replied the old woman. Lady Wang spat in disgust. “If a woman like that is dead, then let her be dead. Is it really worth making such a commotion over?” “She did not die a natural death,” said the old woman. “She died in the course of a terrible uproar. Please, madam, send someone quickly to deal with it.” With that, she made to leave. Lady Wang, both angry and amused, said, “What an impossible old fool she is! Lian, you had better go over and see for yourself. Pay no attention to that muddleheaded creature.” The old woman failed to hear that someone was to be sent; she caught only the words about paying no attention to her and ran home in a huff. Meanwhile, Aunt Xue was waiting anxiously and could hardly bear the delay. When at last she saw the old woman return, she asked, “Whom is her ladyship sending?” The old woman sighed. “Nothing is worse than finding yourself in dire trouble. However close your relatives may be, it seems they are no use at all. Not only did her ladyship refuse to help us, she even called me muddleheaded.” Aunt Xue grew both angry and anxious. “Even if her ladyship will not help, what did our young mistress say?” The old woman replied, “Since her ladyship would not help, naturally our young mistress would be even less likely to. I did not go and tell her.” Aunt Xue spat indignantly. “Her ladyship is an outsider, but that girl is my own daughter. How could she refuse to help?” The old woman suddenly understood. “Why, of course! In that case, I shall go and tell her now.”

p.src: As they were speaking, Jia Lian arrived. After paying his respects to Aunt Xue and expressing his condolences, he said, “My aunt heard that my brother’s wife had died, but however she questioned the old woman, she could get no clear account. She was terribly anxious and sent me to learn exactly what happened, telling me to stay and see to matters here. Whatever needs to be done, Aunt, you have only to tell me, and I shall see to it.” Aunt Xue had been so angry that she could only weep dry tears, but at Jia Lian’s words she smiled and said, “Then I must trouble you, Second Master. I knew your aunt had always treated us with the greatest kindness. It was all because that old fool could not explain matters properly and nearly ruined everything. Please sit down, Second Master, and let me tell you everything slowly.” She continued, “It is nothing else; the trouble is that my daughter-in-law did not die a natural death.” Jia Lian said, “Could she have died in despair over my brother’s conviction?” “If only that were so,” said Aunt Xue. At the beginning of these past few months, she made a mad commotion every day, with her hair dishevelled and her feet bare. Later, when she heard that your brother had been sentenced to death, she wept once, but afterward she actually began painting and powdering her face again. Whenever I remonstrated with her, she raised a dreadful quarrel, so I simply paid her no attention. Then one day, for some reason, she demanded that Xiangling be sent to keep her company. I said, ‘You already have Baochan; what do you need Xiangling for? Besides, you have never liked her, so why invite fresh vexation?’ But she would not relent. With no other choice, I told Xiangling to go to her room. Poor Xiangling dared not disobey me and went despite her illness. To my surprise, she treated Xiangling very well, which pleased me. When your elder cousin heard of it, she said, ‘I fear her intentions may not be good.’ But I took no notice. A few days ago, when Xiangling was ill, she personally made her some soup. But ill-fated Xiangling never got to drink it: just as the bowl was brought before her, my daughter-in-law scalded her own hand and even dropped and smashed the bowl. I was certain she would take her anger out on Xiangling, but she did not lose her temper. She swept up the pieces herself, rinsed the floor clean with water, and the two of them remained on good terms. Last night she again told Baochan to prepare two bowls of soup, saying that she would drink it together with Xiangling. After a while, we heard both her feet thumping inside the room. Baochan began shouting frantically, and then Xiangling too cried out as she came leaning against the wall to summon help. I hurried in and saw blood streaming from my daughter-in-law’s nose and eyes. She was rolling wildly on the floor, clawing at her chest with both hands and kicking her legs. I nearly died of fright. When I questioned her, she could not speak and only kept screaming; after a spell of this commotion, she died. From the look of it, I thought she had taken poison. Baochan then came weeping and seized Xiangling, accusing her of poisoning and killing her mistress. But Xiangling does not seem capable of such a deed to me; besides, she was so ill she could scarcely get up, so how could she have poisoned anyone?

p.src: Yet Baochan stubbornly insisted that it was she. Oh, Second Master, what was I to do? I had no choice but to harden my heart and order the old women to bind Xiangling and hand her over to Baochan; then they fastened the door from outside. Your second cousin and I kept watch all night and did not send word to the mansion until its gates opened. You are a sensible man, Second Master. What is to be done about this?” Jia Lian asked, “Does the Xia family know yet?” Aunt Xue replied, “We must first disentangle the matter before we can properly inform them.” Jia Lian said, “In my view, this can only be settled by taking it before the authorities. We naturally suspect Baochan, but others will ask why Baochan would poison her own mistress, and we have no answer for that. But if the blame is laid on Xiangling, the story appears to fit.” While they were speaking, some women from the Rong mansion entered and announced, “Our Second Young Mistress has arrived.” Although Jia Lian was her elder brother-in-law, they had known each other since childhood, so he did not withdraw. Baochai entered, greeted her mother and Jia Lian, then went into the inner room and sat down with Baoqin. Aunt Xue recounted the whole affair to her as well. Baochai said, “By binding Xiangling, are we not declaring that we too believe she poisoned her mistress? Mother says Baochan made the soup, so Baochan ought to be bound and questioned. We should send someone to inform the Xia family at once and report the matter to the authorities at the same time.” Aunt Xue saw the sense in this and asked Jia Lian what he thought. Jia Lian replied, “My second cousin is quite right. I shall have to make the report myself and enlist the help of acquaintances in the Ministry of Justice, so that someone will look after our interests during the inquest and the taking of statements. I only fear it may be difficult to bind Baochan and release Xiangling.” Aunt Xue said, “It was not that I wanted Xiangling bound. I feared that, being ill and now unjustly accused and distressed, she might suddenly kill herself and add another death to this affair. That was why I had her bound and placed in Baochan’s charge; it seemed one way of keeping her safe.” Jia Lian said, “Even so, we have in effect helped Baochan. If anyone is released, release them all; if anyone is bound, bind them all, for the three were together. We need only have someone comfort Xiangling.” Aunt Xue ordered the door opened, and Baochai directed several women who had accompanied her to help bind Baochan. They found Xiangling weeping herself nearly to death, while Baochan looked positively triumphant. But when Baochan saw that they meant to bind her, she began shouting wildly. She was no match for the women from the Rong mansion, who shouted her down and bound her. They left the door wide open so that everyone could keep watch. Meanwhile, the messenger sent to inform the Xia family had already departed.

p.src: The Xia family had not formerly lived in the capital, but as their fortunes had declined in recent years and they missed their daughter, they had lately moved there. The father was dead, leaving only the mother, who had adopted a worthless son; he had squandered the whole family estate and was forever visiting the Xue household. Jingui was fickle and wanton by nature and could hardly endure an empty bed; moreover, she pined for Xue Ke day after day, until she was nearly desperate enough to take anyone she could get. Unfortunately, this nominal brother of hers was a fool. Though he had begun to sense her meaning, matters had not yet gone any further. Thus Jingui often went home and also gave him some money to help him along. Just then he was eagerly awaiting Jingui's return, and when he saw someone from the Xue household arrive, he wondered what she had sent him this time. But when he was told that the young mistress had died from poison, he flew into a rage and began shouting wildly. When Jingui's mother heard the news, she wailed even louder. “My daughter was perfectly well in their house! Why would she take poison?” Still weeping and shouting, she took her son with her and, too impatient even to wait for a hired cart, set off at once. The Xias had once been a merchant family, but now that their money was gone, they cared nothing for appearances. The son went ahead, while she left the house with a decrepit old woman, tearfully hired a ramshackle cart in the street, and hurried to the Xue residence.

p.src: The moment they entered, without a word of inquiry, they screamed abuse and demanded a life for a life. At the time Jia Lian had gone to the Ministry of Justice to seek assistance, and only Aunt Xue, Baochai, and Baoqin were at home. Never having witnessed such a scene, they were too frightened to utter a sound. When they tried to reason with the newcomers, the pair refused to listen and merely cried, “What good did our daughter ever receive in your house? Husband and wife were quarrelling and cursing from dawn till dusk. After all that uproar, you would not even let the couple stay together. You conspired to have your son-in-law thrown into prison so that they could never meet again. It was not enough that you women could enjoy the protection of powerful relatives; you still found her an eyesore and had someone poison her to death, then claimed she had taken poison herself! Why would she ever take poison?” With that, she charged straight at Aunt Xue. Aunt Xue could only retreat, saying, “Madam Xia, first go and see your daughter and question Baochan. There will be time enough afterward for these slanders.” Because the Xia woman's son was outside, Baochai and Baoqin could not properly come out to protect her and could only fret within. Just then Lady Wang sent Zhou Rui's wife over to see how matters stood. As soon as she entered, she saw an old woman pointing in Aunt Xue's face as she wept and cursed. Zhou Rui's wife guessed that this must be Jingui's mother and went up to her. “Are you Madam Xia?” she asked. The young mistress took poison and died by her own hand. What has that to do with our Aunt Xue? There is no call for you to abuse her so.” “Who are you?” demanded Jingui's mother. Aunt Xue, emboldened somewhat by the arrival of an ally, replied, “She belongs to the Jia household, the family of my relatives.” “Everyone knows you have powerful relatives to back you,” said Jingui's mother. “That is how you managed to have your son-in-law put in prison. And now is my daughter to have died for nothing?” As she spoke, she seized Aunt Xue. “Tell me exactly how you killed my daughter! Let me see her!” “You may certainly see her,” Zhou Rui's wife said as she tried to calm the woman, “but there is no need for all this pulling and tugging.” Then she pushed the woman's hand away. The Xia woman's son rushed in and protested, “Are you relying on the power of the Jia household to strike my mother?” With that, he hurled a chair at her, but missed. When Baochai's attendants inside heard the commotion, they hurried out to see what was happening. Fearing that Zhou Rui's wife might suffer at their hands, they crowded forward together, half coaxing and half scolding. At this, the Xia woman and her son abandoned all restraint and made a full-blown scene. “We know how powerful your Rong mansion is! Our daughter is already dead, and now neither of us cares whether we live or die!” So saying, they again charged at Aunt Xue, ready to fight to the death. Though there were many people present, they could not hold the pair back. As the old saying goes, “When one man stakes his life, ten thousand cannot withstand him.”

p.src: Just as the uproar reached a dangerous pitch, Jia Lian entered with seven or eight servants. Seeing the situation, he first ordered them to drag the Xia woman's son outside, then said, “Stop this disturbance. If you have something to say, say it calmly. Quickly put the house in order. The officials from the Ministry of Justice will soon be here to conduct the inquest.” Jingui's mother was still raging when she saw a gentleman arrive, with several men clearing the way before him and all the others standing respectfully with hands lowered. Seeing this display, Jingui's mother did not know which member of the Jia family he was. But her son had already been seized, and she had heard that the Ministry of Justice was coming to conduct an inquest. She had originally meant to see her daughter's corpse, create utter havoc, and then appeal to the authorities; she had never expected the Xues to report the case first, and so her bluster somewhat subsided. Aunt Xue was already senseless with fright. It was Zhou Rui's wife who reported what had happened. “They came here and, without even going to see their daughter, began abusing Aunt Xue. When we tried to reason with her for her own good, this wild fellow came charging into the women's quarters, shouting obscenities and striking out at everyone. Is there no law left in the land?” Jia Lian said, “There is no need to reason with him now. When the time comes, beat him while you question him: a man has his proper place, while the inner quarters are full of young ladies and married women. Besides, with his mother here, could he not trust her to see their young mistress? If he burst in like that, was it not to assault and rob the household?” With a mixture of coaxing and threats, the servants finally subdued them. Emboldened by their greater numbers, Zhou Rui's wife said, “Madam Xia, you are behaving most unreasonably. Since you have come, you ought first to find out exactly what happened. Your daughter either took poison and died by her own hand, or Baochan poisoned her mistress. Yet without asking what happened or even viewing the corpse, you came here intending to extort money. Do you suppose we would willingly let a daughter-in-law of this family die for nothing? Baochan is now tied up. Since your daughter was certain to accuse Xiangling of something, we had Xiangling stay with Baochan in the same room, and both of them are being guarded there. We were waiting for you to come and witness the Ministry's inquest with your own eyes, so that the truth might be established through questioning.”

u.src: Just as the uproar reached a dangerous pitch, Jia Lian entered with seven or eight servants. Seeing the situation, he first ordered them to drag the Xia woman's son outside, then said, “Stop this disturbance. If you have something to say, say it calmly.
Quickly put the house in order. The officials from the Ministry of Justice will soon be here to conduct the inquest.”
Jingui's mother was still raging when she saw a gentleman arrive, with several men clearing the way before him and all the others standing respectfully with hands lowered.

Seeing this display, Jingui's mother did not know which member of the Jia family he was. But her son had already been seized, and she had heard that the Ministry of Justice was coming to conduct an inquest. She had originally meant to see her daughter's corpse, create utter havoc, and then appeal to the authorities; she had never expected the Xues to report the case first, and so her bluster somewhat subsided.
Aunt Xue was already senseless with fright.
It was Zhou Rui's wife who reported what had happened. “They came here and, without even going to see their daughter, began abusing Aunt Xue.
When we tried to reason with her for her own good, this wild fellow came charging into the women's quarters, shouting obscenities and striking out at everyone. Is there no law left in the land?”

Jia Lian said, “There is no need to reason with him now. When the time comes, beat him while you question him: a man has his proper place, while the inner quarters are full of young ladies and married women. Besides, with his mother here, could he not trust her to see their young mistress? If he burst in like that, was it not to assault and rob the household?”
With a mixture of coaxing and threats, the servants finally subdued them.
Emboldened by their greater numbers, Zhou Rui's wife said, “Madam Xia, you are behaving most unreasonably. Since you have come, you ought first to find out exactly what happened.

Your daughter either took poison and died by her own hand, or Baochan poisoned her mistress. Yet without asking what happened or even viewing the corpse, you came here intending to extort money. Do you suppose we would willingly let a daughter-in-law of this family die for nothing?

Baochan is now tied up. Since your daughter was certain to accuse Xiangling of something, we had Xiangling stay with Baochan in the same room, and both of them are being guarded there. We were waiting for you to come and witness the Ministry's inquest with your own eyes, so that the truth might be established through questioning.”

p.src: Jin-gui's mother, now isolated and powerless, had no choice but to follow Zhou Rui's wife into her daughter's room. There she saw Jin-gui lying rigid on the kang, her face covered in black blood, and immediately began to wail. When Baochan saw that members of Jin-gui's family had arrived, she cried out through her tears, “Our mistress treated Xiangling kindly and let her live with her, but Xiangling seized her chance and poisoned our mistress to death!” All the Xue household, high and low, were present by then, and they shouted in unison, “Nonsense! Mistress Jin-gui died only after drinking the soup yesterday—and weren't you the one who made it?” Baochan replied, “I did make the soup, but after bringing it in I had business elsewhere and left. I don't know what Xiangling got up and put into it to poison our mistress.” Before she had finished, Jin-gui's mother lunged at Xiangling. The others held her back. Aunt Xue said, “From the look of her, she was poisoned with arsenic, and there is certainly no such substance in this house. Whether it was Xiangling or Baochan, someone must have bought it for her. Once the Ministry of Justice investigates, the truth is bound to come out, and no one will be able to deny it. For now, lay my daughter-in-law out properly so that she will be ready for the officials' examination.” The old serving-women came forward and laid the body out. Baochai said, “Since men will be coming in, go through and put in order all the things used by the women.” Under the bedding on the kang they found a paper packet crumpled into a ball. Jin-gui's mother spotted it and picked it up. Finding nothing inside when she opened it, she tossed it aside. Baochan saw it and said, “There—surely that is evidence! I recognize that paper packet. A few days ago, when the mice were causing trouble, Mistress Jin-gui went home and asked her brother for it. She brought it back and put it in her jewel box. Xiangling must have seen it, taken it, and used it to poison her. If you do not believe me, look in the jewel box and see whether it is still there.”

p.src: Following Baochan's directions, Jin-gui's mother took out the box, but there were only a few silver hairpins inside. Aunt Xue said, “Why are so many pieces of jewelry missing?” Baochai had the chests and cupboards opened, but they were all empty. She said, “If we want to know who took Sister-in-law's things, we shall have to ask Baochan.” Jin-gui's mother grew much less sure of herself. Seeing Aunt Xue question Baochan, she said, “How would the girl know what belonged to her mistress?” Zhou Rui's wife said, “Madam in-law, you must not say that. I know that Baochan attended Mistress Jin-gui every day. How can you say she knows nothing?” Pressed so closely and unable simply to fabricate a denial, Baochan had to say, “Mistress Jin-gui often took the things back to her mother's home herself. How could I stop her?” Everyone exclaimed, “What a fine in-law you are! You coaxed her into bringing you her things, and when you had taken everything, you told her to kill herself so that you could extort money from us. Very well—when the officials come to examine the body, that is exactly what we shall tell them.” Baochai ordered someone, “Go outside and tell Second Master Lian not to let any of the Xia family leave.”

p.src: Inside, Jin-gui's mother was thrown into a panic and cursed Baochan: “You little slut, stop wagging your tongue! When did my daughter ever take those things to my house?” Baochan replied, “The property is a small matter now; the great matter is that someone must answer with her life for Mistress Jin-gui's death.” Baoqin said, “Once the property is traced, we shall also find the person who must answer for her life. Quickly ask Second Brother Lian to confirm the account of the Xia family's son buying arsenic, so that later we can answer the Ministry of Justice.” Jin-gui's mother anxiously exclaimed, “Baochan must be possessed by a ghost to babble such nonsense! My daughter never bought arsenic! If that is what she claims, then Baochan herself must have poisoned my daughter.” Baochan, frantic with anger, shouted, “It would be one thing for other people to blame me, but how can even you turn around and accuse me? Didn't you constantly tell Mistress Jin-gui not to submit to any wrong, but to bring their household to ruin, then bundle up the property and leave, so that afterward she could marry a better husband? Did you say those words or not?” Before Jin-gui's mother could answer, Zhou Rui's wife cut in: “Those words came from one of your own household. What is left for you to deny?” Gnashing her teeth with hatred, Jin-gui's mother cursed Baochan: “I have treated you well! Why do you turn my own words against me and seek to destroy me? When we appear before the officials, I shall tell them that you poisoned my daughter to death.” Baochan glared at her furiously and said, “Madam, please let Xiangling go. There is no reason to harm an innocent person. I shall know what to say when I face the officials.”

p.src: Baochai understood what lay behind these words and instead ordered Baochan to be released. “You have always been a forthright person. Why suffer unjustly for nothing? If you have something to say, say it outright. Once everything is clear to us all, will that not settle the matter?” Baochan, also afraid of the suffering she would endure before the authorities, said, “Every day our mistress complained, ‘How could a woman like me have been saddled with such a blind fool of a mother? Instead of marrying me to Second Master Bao, she gave me to that muddleheaded good-for-nothing. If I could spend even one day with Second Master Bao, I would willingly die afterward.’ Whenever she spoke of this, she would turn her hatred upon Xiangling. At first I paid no attention. Later, when I saw her treating Xiangling kindly, I thought Xiangling must have put some idea into her head. I never imagined yesterday’s soup had been offered with evil intent.” Jingui’s mother cut in, “Now you are talking even greater nonsense! If she meant to poison Xiangling, why did she poison herself instead?” Baochai then asked, “Xiangling, did you drink any soup yesterday?” Xiangling replied, “A few days ago I was so ill I could not lift my head. When Mistress told me to drink some soup, I did not dare refuse. Just as I struggled to sit up, the bowl was spilled, making Mistress clean up the mess, and I felt terribly sorry. Yesterday, when I heard that I was to drink soup again, I could not stomach it, but there was no help for it. Just as I was about to drink, I happened to grow dizzy again. I saw Sister Baochan carry it away and was secretly relieved. I had just closed my eyes when Mistress, drinking soup herself, told me to taste some, so I forced myself to drink it too.” Before Xiangling had finished, Baochan said, “That explains it. I will tell you the whole truth. Yesterday Mistress told me to prepare two bowls of soup, saying that she and Xiangling would drink them together. I was indignant, thinking Xiangling was hardly worthy of having me make soup for her. So I deliberately threw an extra handful of salt into one bowl and marked it secretly, intending it for Xiangling. I had just carried the bowls in when Mistress stopped me and sent me outside to tell the lads to hire a cart, saying that she would return home that day. After delivering the message, I came back and saw the saltier bowl before Mistress. I was afraid she would taste how salty it was and scold me again. While I was at a loss, Mistress walked toward the back. The instant she was out of sight, I exchanged her bowl for Xiangling’s. Fate must have ordained it so: when Mistress returned, she took the soup to Xiangling’s bedside and drank from it, saying, ‘You really must taste some.’ Xiangling did not find it salty either. The two of them drank it all. I was laughing at Xiangling for having no palate. How could I have known that our wretched dead mistress meant to poison her and must have sprinkled arsenic into the soup while I was away? She never knew I had exchanged the bowls. Heaven’s justice is manifest indeed: she brought destruction upon herself.”

p.src: Everyone then considered the events from beginning to end and found that every detail fitted perfectly. They released Xiangling as well and helped her back onto the bed to rest.

p.src: We shall leave Xiangling after her release and speak instead of Jingui’s mother, who, though inwardly conscious of the truth, still tried to argue and deny it. Aunt Xue and the others answered her one after another, demanding instead that her son pay with his life for Jingui’s death. In the midst of the uproar, Jia Lian shouted from outside, “There is no use saying any more. Make everything ready at once—the officials from the Board of Punishments will soon be here.” At this, only the Xia mother and son grew alarmed. Realizing they were bound to come off worst, they had no choice but to plead with Aunt Xue instead: “However many wrongs were committed, in the end it was my wretched dead daughter who lacked good sense. She merely reaped what she had sown. If the Board of Punishments conducts an inquest, it will after all reflect poorly on your household. I beg you, dear in-law, to let the matter rest.” Baochai said, “That is impossible. It has already been reported; how can it now be suppressed?” Zhou Rui’s wife and the others alternately coaxed and admonished her: “If you want the matter dropped, the only way is for Madam Xia herself to go out and prevent the inquest. We shall then say nothing about who was right or wrong.” Outside, Jia Lian also intimidated her son into submission, and he agreed to meet the officials from the Board of Punishments and sign a bond declining the inquest. Everyone agreed to this arrangement. Aunt Xue ordered servants to purchase a coffin and encoffin the body. We shall say no more of this.

p.src: Now Jia Yucun had been promoted to governor of the metropolitan prefecture, with concurrent charge of taxation. One day he left the capital to inspect newly reclaimed lands and, passing through Zhiji County, arrived at Rushing Current Ford. Just as he was about to cross to the opposite bank, he had his sedan chair set down while he waited for bearers. Beside the village he saw a small temple whose walls had crumbled away, revealing several ancient pines, venerable and weathered in appearance. Yucun stepped out of his chair and strolled into the temple. The gilding had peeled from the divine images, the halls leaned askew, and beside them stood a broken stone tablet whose blurred inscription he could not decipher. He was about to proceed to the rear hall when he saw a thatched hut shaded by a green cypress. Inside it, a Taoist sat meditating with his eyes closed. When Yucun approached and looked at him, the face seemed very familiar. He felt sure he had seen the man somewhere before, but for the moment could not recall where. His attendants were about to shout at the Taoist. Yucun restrained them, walked slowly forward, and called, “Reverend Taoist.” The Taoist opened his eyes slightly and asked with a faint smile, “What business brings Your Excellency here?” Yucun replied, “I have left the capital on official business to conduct an inspection. Passing this place, I saw how serenely you pursue your cultivation and supposed that you must possess profound mastery of the Way. I have therefore ventured to ask your instruction.” The Taoist said, “One comes from a destined place and goes in a destined direction.” Realizing that the man was no ordinary person, Yucun bowed deeply and asked, “Where did you cultivate the Way before building your hut here? What is the name of this temple? How many people live within it? If you seek true cultivation, are there no famous mountains? If you seek ties with others, why not dwell beside a busy thoroughfare?” The Taoist replied, “If even a gourd can shelter the body, why must one build a dwelling on a famous mountain? The temple’s name has long been hidden, yet the broken tablet still remains. With form and shadow keeping each other company, what need is there to build or solicit alms? How could I resemble those of whom it was said, ‘Jade in its casket seeks a worthy price, while the hairpin in its case awaits the time to fly’?”

p.src: Yucun was naturally quick-witted. First he heard the word “gourd,” and then the paired names “Jade” and “Hairpin”; suddenly, the affair of Zhen Shiyin came back to him. He scrutinized the Taoist once more and, seeing that his features were unchanged, dismissed his attendants and asked, “Can you possibly be the venerable Mr. Zhen?” The Taoist smiled calmly. “What is true, and what is false? You must understand that truth is falsehood, and falsehood truth.” Hearing him utter the word “Jia,” Yucun’s doubts vanished entirely. He saluted him anew and said, “Ever since you generously enabled me to reach the capital, I have enjoyed your protection: I distinguished myself in the civil examinations and received an appointment in your honored district. Only then did I learn that you had transcended the mortal world and ascended to the realm of immortals. Though I longed ardently to seek you out, I reflected that I was merely a worldly official and had no means of beholding your immortal countenance again. How fortunate I am to meet you here today! I beg you, venerable immortal, to enlighten me in my ignorance. If you would not disdain me, my residence in the capital is quite near. I could attend upon you there and receive your instruction morning and evening.” The Taoist also rose and returned his salute. “Beyond my meditation cushion, I know not what else may exist between heaven and earth. I understand not a word of what Your Excellency has just said.” Having said this, he sat down again as before. Yucun’s doubts returned. “If he is not Shiyin, why do his face and speech resemble his so closely? Nineteen years have passed since we parted, yet his complexion remains unchanged. He must have perfected his cultivation and be unwilling to disclose his former identity. But having met my benefactor, I cannot let him slip away before my very eyes. Plainly, wealth and rank will not move him; still less need I mention such private matters as his wife and daughter.” Having reached this conclusion, he said, “Since my immortal master refuses to reveal the causes of the past, how can this disciple bear it in his heart?” Just as he was about to prostrate himself, an attendant entered and reported that evening was approaching, urging him to cross the river at once. While Yucun stood irresolute, the Taoist said, “Your Excellency should hasten to the farther shore. We shall have occasion to meet again; delay, and the wind and waves will suddenly rise. If you truly do not disdain me, I shall await your instruction here at the ferry another day.” With that, he closed his eyes and resumed his meditation. Yucun had no choice but to take his leave of the Taoist and quit the temple. Just as he was about to cross the river, he saw someone come racing toward him. What business brought him there remains unknown; the next chapter will reveal it.

While Yucun stood irresolute, the Taoist said, “Your Excellency should hasten to the farther shore. We shall have occasion to meet again; delay, and the wind and waves will suddenly rise.
If you truly do not disdain me, I shall await your instruction here at the ferry another day.”
With that, he closed his eyes and resumed his meditation.
Yucun had no choice but to take his leave of the Taoist and quit the temple.
Just as he was about to cross the river, he saw someone come racing toward him.
What business brought him there remains unknown; the next chapter will reveal it.
